CSP Provider.content:
Published API for quoin-ui/csp-provider at 0.6.0. Imports in these declarations are relative to the linked original files.

Source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/quoin-ui@0.6.0/dist/csp-provider/index.d.ts

```ts
export type { CSPProviderProps } from "./csp-provider.js";
export { CSPContext, type CSPContextValue, NOOP_CSP_CONTEXT, Provider as CSPProvider, useCSPContext, useCspDisableStyleElements, useCspNonce, } from "./index.parts.js";
```

Source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/quoin-ui@0.6.0/dist/csp-provider/index.parts.d.ts

```ts
export { CSPContext, type CSPContextValue, NOOP_CSP_CONTEXT, useCSPContext, useCspDisableStyleElements, useCspNonce, } from "./csp-context.js";
export { CSPProvider as Provider } from "./csp-provider.js";
```

Source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/quoin-ui@0.6.0/dist/csp-provider/csp-context.d.ts

```ts
import { type Accessor } from "solid-js";
/**
 * The value handed down by `<CSPProvider>` to its descendants.
 *
 * `nonce` is an accessor so a parent that updates `props.nonce` is observed
 * by consumers without them needing to subscribe to an outer signal — this
 * keeps the shape consistent with the other Base UI internal contexts (see
 * `field-context.ts`) and avoids the top-level reactive-read warning in
 * Solid 2.
 *
 * `disableStyleElements` mirrors React Base UI's CSP context flag: when
 * `true`, components skip injecting inline `<style>` tags (e.g. the
 * scroll-area's disable-scrollbar stylesheet). Callers opt in when their
 * CSP forbids inline style elements even with a nonce, and provide the
 * styles through an external stylesheet instead.
 */
export interface CSPContextValue {
    nonce: Accessor<string | undefined>;
    disableStyleElements: Accessor<boolean>;
}
export declare const NOOP_CSP_CONTEXT: CSPContextValue;
/**
 * Context carrying the CSP nonce. Provide it with `<CSPContext value={...}>`
 * (Solid 2's context-as-provider pattern — there is no `.Provider`).
 */
export declare const CSPContext: import("solid-js").Context<CSPContextValue>;
/**
 * Read the current CSP context. When no `<CSPProvider>` is above, returns
 * the noop context whose accessors yield sensible defaults (`undefined`
 * nonce, `false` disable-style-elements).
 */
export declare function useCSPContext(): CSPContextValue;
/**
 * Convenience helper — read the nonce as an accessor, decoupled from the
 * shape of the context value. Consumers that only need the nonce should
 * prefer this so they aren't re-subscribed when unrelated CSP fields are
 * added to the context in the future.
 */
export declare function useCspNonce(): Accessor<string | undefined>;
/**
 * Convenience helper — read the `disableStyleElements` flag as an accessor.
 */
export declare function useCspDisableStyleElements(): Accessor<boolean>;
```

Source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/quoin-ui@0.6.0/dist/csp-provider/csp-provider.d.ts

```ts
import type { JSX } from "@solidjs/web";
export interface CSPProviderProps {
    children?: JSX.Element;
    /**
     * The nonce value to apply to inline `<style>` and `<script>` tags
     * injected by Base UI components for CSP compliance.
     */
    nonce?: string | undefined;
    /**
     * When `true`, descendants skip injecting inline `<style>` elements
     * (e.g. the scroll-area's disable-scrollbar stylesheet). Use when your
     * CSP forbids inline styles outright, even with a valid nonce, and
     * provide the styles through an external stylesheet instead.
     *
     * @default false
     */
    disableStyleElements?: boolean | undefined;
}
/**
 * Provides a Content Security Policy (CSP) nonce that Base UI components
 * attach to inline `<style>` and `<script>` tags.
 *
 * Solid 2 uses the context value itself as the provider component (no
 * `.Provider`). The context value is a plain object with a getter so the
 * `nonce` accessor tracks `props.nonce` without a top-level reactive read.
 */
export declare function CSPProvider(props: CSPProviderProps): JSX.Element;
```

Source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/quoin-ui@0.6.0/dist/direction-provider/direction-provider-context.d.ts

```ts
import { type Accessor } from "solid-js";
export type TextDirection = "ltr" | "rtl";
/**
 * Context carrying the current text direction as an `Accessor`. Provided via
 * Solid 2's context-as-provider pattern:
 * `<DirectionContext value={() => direction}>`.
 *
 * @internal
 */
export declare const DirectionContext: import("solid-js").Context<Accessor<TextDirection>>;
/**
 * Read the current text direction. Returns an `Accessor<TextDirection>` so
 * consumers stay reactive; call it (e.g. `useDirection()()`) to get the
 * current value. Defaults to `"ltr"` when no provider is mounted.
 */
export declare function useDirection(): Accessor<TextDirection>;
```

Source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/quoin-ui@0.6.0/dist/direction-provider/direction-provider.d.ts

```ts
import type { JSX } from "@solidjs/web";
import { type TextDirection } from "./direction-provider-context.js";
export interface DirectionProviderProps {
    children?: JSX.Element;
    /**
     * The reading direction of the text.
     * @default "ltr"
     */
    direction?: TextDirection | undefined;
}
/**
 * Enables RTL behavior for Base UI components.
 *
 * Documentation: [Base UI Direction Provider](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/direction-provider)
 */
export declare function DirectionProvider(props: DirectionProviderProps): JSX.Element;
```

Form.content:
Published API for quoin-ui/form at 0.6.0. Imports in these declarations are relative to the linked original files.

Source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/quoin-ui@0.6.0/dist/form/index.d.ts

```ts
export type { FormContextValue, FormErrors, FormFieldEntry, FormProps, FormState, FormValidationMode, } from "./form.js";
export { Form } from "./form.js";
```

Source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/quoin-ui@0.6.0/dist/form/form.d.ts

```ts
import type { JSX, ValidComponent } from "@solidjs/web";
import type { FieldValidationMode } from "../internals/field-constants.js";
import { type FormContextValue, type FormErrors, type FormFieldEntry } from "../internals/form-context.js";
import type { BaseUIComponentProps } from "../internals/types.js";
export type { FormContextValue, FormErrors, FormFieldEntry };
export type FormValidationMode = FieldValidationMode;
export type FormState = Record<string, never>;
export interface FormProps extends BaseUIComponentProps<"form", FormState> {
    /**
     * Tag/component to render. Defaults to `"form"`.
     */
    as?: ValidComponent;
    /**
     * Determines when the form should be validated. The `validationMode`
     * prop on `<Field.Root>` takes precedence over this.
     *
     * @default "onSubmit"
     */
    validationMode?: FormValidationMode | undefined;
    /**
     * Validation errors returned externally (e.g. from server submission).
     * Keys correspond to `<Field.Root>`'s `name` attribute; values are the
     * error(s) for that field.
     */
    errors?: FormErrors | undefined;
    /**
     * Called when the consumer submits the form AND every registered field
     * passed validation. The native submit event is passed through — the
     * consumer is free to call `preventDefault()` as needed.
     */
    onSubmit?: JSX.EventHandler<HTMLFormElement, SubmitEvent> | undefined;
    /**
     * Called when submission is blocked because one or more registered
     * fields failed validation. Base UI already calls `preventDefault()` on
     * the submit event before invoking this handler.
     */
    onSubmitValidationFailed?: ((event: SubmitEvent, invalidFields: FormFieldEntry[]) => void) | undefined;
}
/**
 * A native `<form>` element that coordinates cross-field validation with
 * any `<Field.Root>` descendants.
 *
 * On native submit:
 *   1. Flip `submitAttemptedRef.current` to `true`.
 *   2. Iterate `formRef.current.fields` and call each field's `validate`.
 *   3. If any field reports `validityData.state.valid === false`, call
 *      `preventDefault()` on the submit event and invoke
 *      `onSubmitValidationFailed`.
 *   4. Otherwise pass the event through to the consumer's `onSubmit`.
 *
 * On native reset: clear the internal error map and reset
 * `submitAttemptedRef`.
 *
 * Documentation: [Base UI Form](https://base-ui.com/react/components/form)
 */
export declare function Form(props: FormProps): JSX.Element;
```
